newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian minister seen withdrawing OAU candidacy.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian minister seen withdrawing OAU candidacy.

text.p: Ivory Coast is expected to withdraw Foreign Minister Amara Essy's candidacy for the top job at the Organisation of African Unity, leaving the way clear for incumbent Salim Ahmed Salim to take a third term, political sources said on Wednesday.

The sources said the government felt Essy's chances of election were reduced as his support was essentially from francophone countries, many of which are in arrears to the organisation and would not be allowed to vote. They said Salim's candidacy benefitted from the support of South Africa.
Essy refused to confirm or deny the speculation that he would withdraw. "It is up to the government to announce the Ivorian position at the right time," he told Reuters.
The long-serving and respected minister was president of the United Nations General Assembly from 1994 to 1995. He was Kofi Annan's closest rival for the post of U.N. secretary-general last year.
Salim, a former Tanzanian foreign minister and diplomat, has headed the 53-member OAU since 1989 and is seeking a third four-year term at an OAU summit in Zimbabwe next week.
